title: The collection of weights of generalized metric tree arrangements is the Dressian Dr(k,n)
author: Ayush Kumar Tewari
work: Generalized metric tree arrangements and Dressians
source_version: arXiv:2210.06868v2 (CC BY 4.0); v3 withdrawn by arXiv admin
difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the headline result of the article's fourth section and of its abstract, and its twelve-line author proof is a genuine research-level set equality rather than a qualification exercise. Even with the whole apparatus of the delivered context supplied - the Dressian Dr(k,n) as the tropical prevariety of the three-term Plucker relations, the phylogenetic and tree-distance definitions, the definition of a metric tree arrangement and of an abstract tree arrangement, Lemma lem:mat_sub_k,n with its complete proof, and above all the author's own definition of a generalized metric tree arrangement with its compatibility equation and the induced weight vector w_T - the solver must still do the following. For the forward inclusion it must recognise that a fixed three-term tropical Plucker relation for Dr(k,n) is indexed by a (k-2)-subset J together with four distinct indices outside J, identify the family S of k-subsets containing J, observe that S is in bijection with the two-subsets of the complement of J so that the restriction of w_T to those Plucker variables is exactly the weight induced by the single metric tree T_J, and then import Speyer-Sturmfels' identification of the weights induced by metric trees on n-k+2 leaves with Dr(2,n-k+2) in order to conclude that the maximum of the relation is attained by at least two of its three terms. For the reverse inclusion it must run the construction the other way: from an arbitrary w in Dr(k,n), restrict w along each (k-2)-subset J, read the restricted Plucker variables as a weight on the two-subsets of the complement of J, obtain a point of Dr(2,n-k+2), invoke the same metric-tree representation to produce a tree T_J on those leaves, and then verify that the resulting family of trees satisfies the compatibility condition - which is the point where the author's definition has to be recognised as having been designed to make w_T well defined, since all the trees are cut out of one and the same point w. This mutual reduction between a single generalized object and a whole family of rank-two Dressians, plus the well-definedness argument that carries the definition, is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations in tropical geometry.
